highlights.content: ![]() ![Invezz](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/invezz--theme-light.svg) ![Invezz](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/invezz--theme-dark.svg) # Nvidia tells data center partners to limit China exposure below 50%: report ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg) ![Jensen Huang](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/image/invezz:e53c09b27094b-0d92e7daf13332cdb6119771fa1ebd69-resized.webp) Nvidia NVDA has instructed its data center partners to reduce their exposure to Chinese customers, according to a Financial Times report published Tuesday, amid Washington's increasing efforts to restrict Beijing's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips. The world's largest chipmaker has reportedly told cloud computing partners to ensure that at least 51% of their services are sold to non-Chinese companies. The guidance was communicated verbally through Nvidia's sales teams and regional offices rather than through formal written instructions, the report said. The reported restrictions apply to new contracts and do not affect existing agreements. Nvidia has not officially confirmed the policy. **What has Nvidia told its partners?** The reported requirement would push data center operators to diversify their customer base and reduce the proportion of computing services supplied to Chinese businesses. The development could create additional challenges for Chinese AI companies that have relied on overseas cloud providers to access advanced Nvidia processors. Renting computing capacity outside China has offered these companies an alternative route to using powerful American chips without importing them directly. A follow-up report by The Information said Nvidia's instructions were intended to encourage a broader customer mix and were not being enforced as a mandatory restriction. The distinction suggests the company is seeking greater oversight of how its chips are used. **Nvidia defends American chip infrastructure** America cannot win the AI race unless America's AI infrastructure wins worldwide -- if the world's clouds rely on foreign-made chips, the model and application layers will be foreign-built as well. Nvidia neither confirmed nor denied the report. However, the company emphasized the importance of expanding the global reach of American-built AI infrastructure. "Datacenters and clouds built on American chips are the foundation that American model and application makers need to compete worldwide," the company said in a statement cited by AFP. It added that America's ability to compete in AI depends on its infrastructure being widely adopted across global cloud networks. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told AFP that she was unaware of the reported restrictions. She added that Beijing hopes companies from all countries will receive a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory business environment. **Nvidia under scanner** The reported move comes as Washington continues to restrict exports of advanced AI processors to China, citing national security concerns and the potential military applications of the technology. Last week, a New York Times investigation reported that US intelligence officials suspected a Chinese businesswoman associated with Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed of passing commercial information to Beijing. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had reportedly developed a close relationship with the executive. Nvidia has said their interactions were routine business meetings. Separately, a contractor linked to server maker Super Micro pleaded guilty in October to participating in a scheme to illegally divert Nvidia-powered AI servers to China. Prosecutors allege that there are two others associated with Super Micro, including a co-founder of the AI-server ​maker, who conspired to divert about $2.5 billion worth of US AI technology to China in violation ​of export laws. ## [NVDA chart](/chart/?symbol=NASDAQ%3ANVDA) ## [Latest news](/news-flow) ## [More news from Invezz](/news-flow/?provider=inve...

Nvidia remains the largest supplier of GPU chip for AI data centers. Nvidia's stock is already priced for slowing growth, making it a potential buy for long-term investors ahead of its Q3 earnings report this month. The stakes are high this earnings season. Investors are paying close attention to how changes in the debt markets and capital expenditures might impact the artificial intelligence (AI) trade. Fears about a possible slowdown in the AI build-out have already stoked a broad sell-off across AI infrastructure stocks, including data center GPU kingpin **Nvidia**(NASDAQ: NVDA), which now sits about 15% below its all-time high. ***Missed AI’s "Act 1"? "Act 2" is the global rollout. Here's what matters as we approach a very important earnings report. ## The pressure is starting to build even more At this point, Nvidia is probably used to the pressure of being the face of the AI infrastructure trade. But as speculation rises over whether funding will dry up for companies building all these data centers -- you know, Nvidia's customers -- the pressure is going to turn up even more. ![Nvidia company graphic.](https://barchart-news-media-prod.aws.barchart.com/FC/173fc6619cefb8dbb5cdb55e5e49e0f6/%3Furl%3Dhttps%253a%252f%252fg.foolcdn.com%252feditorial%252fimages%252f888176%252fnvidia-company-graphic.png%26amp%3Bw%3D700) Image source: The Motley Fool. Buying the stock here at 23 times earnings would probably look like a no-brainer in hindsight if the company actually grows that quickly. And it might. But analysts have begun to lower their expectations as concerns about the state of the infrastructure trade rise. AI Agents.content: [Skip to content](#responsive-grid-main-content) [###### < ALL PRESS RELEASES](/en/news/press-releases/) # Snowflake Helps Enterprises Deploy AI Agents with Trusted Business Context and Built-In Controls ![](/content/dam/snowflake-site/general/static/images/hero-dots.png) ![Snowflake](/adobe/dynamicmedia/deliver/dm-aid--c5365be3-e24d-4d33-8b62-8ee7513f2587/snowflake-business-ontology.png?quality=85&preferwebp=true) *Business Ontology, a part of Snowflake Horizon Catalog, grounds enterprise AI agents in trusted, pre-approved definitions, so every answer is consistent, traceable, and ready for action* ![Snowflake Cortex AI Gateway PR image](/adobe/dynamicmedia/deliver/dm-aid--6b3e979c-9656-4ab3-a68f-63bc33545f7d/snowflake-cortex-ai-gateway.png?quality=85&preferwebp=true) *Cortex AI Gateway, a part of Snowflake Horizon Catalog, brings every agent under a unified set of controls, giving enterprises the visibility to secure and govern AI connections, track usage, and keep AI spending in check* * **Definitions Agents Can't Argue With:** Business Ontology gives organizations one governed place to record what their business terms officially mean across their data estate, and serves only approved definitions to agents * **Every Agent Under One Centralized Control:** Cortex AI Gateway extends Snowflake's security and governance capabilities to all agents to help teams govern and use right-sized models for managing budgets * **Proof Across the Enterprise:** Industry leaders including Glean and Kargo rely on Cortex AI Gateway to govern every AI agent across their business, while companies like dentsu and Merkle use Business Ontology to ground those agents in definitions the business has approved. **SNOWFLAKE EXPEDITION 2026 – Nov. 3, 2026 –** [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/) (NYSE: SNOW), the AI Data Cloud company, today at [Snowflake Expedition 2026](https://www.snowflake.com/en/expedition/) announced new innovations that put context, security, and governance at the foundation of every AI agent, not bolted on after the fact. Snowflake is interoperable by design, connecting an organization's entire data estate across catalogs and clouds, providing the universal governance controls and context that agents and analytics depend on. To bring that same governance and context to autonomous agents, Snowflake is bringing new capabilities to [Horizon Context](https://www.snowflake.com/en/product/features/horizon-context/), the home for governed business context inside [Snowflake Horizon Catalog](https://www.snowflake.com/en/product/features/horizon/). Snowflake’s new [**Business Ontology**](http://www.snowflake.com/en/blog/business-ontology-context)3 allows these agents to operate with a shared, pre-approved understanding of core business definitions to enable reliable answers. While [**Cortex AI Gateway**](https://www.snowflake.com/en/blog/cortex-ai-gateway-control-plane-enterprise-ai/)1 governs how the agents access models, invoke tools, and take action across enterprise systems. As a result, every decision and operation remains secure, fully auditable, and bound to a single set of policies, on a single data copy, regardless of which cloud, catalog, or engine the data sits in. Trusted and reliable agents are hard to build. Not because of model limitations, but because enterprise context is inherently fractured. According to a recent MIT Technology Review [report](https://www.snowflake.com/en/lp/raising-the-quality-of-insights-in-agentic-analytics/) sponsored by Snowflake, **55%** of executives cite a lack of business context as the primary cause of low-quality AI agent insights, with fragmented or inaccessible data ranking second at **45%**. As these agents spread across the business, connecting to models, MCP servers, and enterprise systems, they’re multiplying faster than IT and security can keep up. Companies are left with an impossible choice between scaling AI quickly while absorbing inaccuracies, vulnerabilities, and runaway cost...

Growth is accelerating: **5.4x** vs. **3.9x** a year ago. Based on what we’ve heard from enterprise buyers, companies aren’t pulling back. They’re finding more ways to put AI to work and agents are driving a lot of that demand. If anything, we may still be underestimating just how big this market can become.” ![](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2026/11/menlo-ventures-logo-orange-gray-main-2-300x107.png) “Agents are changing the economics of software. Anthropic grew its share of enterprise API spending from 40% to 55%, while Google fell from 21% to 9%. That’s how quickly the competitive landscape can change. The labs have a tremendous advantage because building frontier models is incredibly hard, but no one’s position is guaranteed. AI Agents.title: Apple warns of AI agents behave in 'unintended or unpredictable' ways
AI Agents.titleZh: Apple warns of AI agents behave in 'unintended or unpredictable' ways
AI Agents.content: In this article Apple said in its annual financial filing on Tuesday that AI agents that can act in "unintended or unpredictable ways" could represent a threat to its business by opening the company up to lawsuits or hurting its reputation. The new risk factors in Apple's filing show the disruptive potential of AI agents, which have rapidly become top of mind for Silicon Valley's most important companies. "In particular, artificial intelligence agents and other technologies can take actions autonomously, including interacting with internal or external systems that in some cases they may not be authorized to access, executing or altering code, sending communications, and completing transactions," Apple wrote in the filing. The company added that agents "may behave in unintended or unpredictable ways, including by taking actions that were not directed, instructed or authorized." Earlier this year, OpenAI released Dots, and Meta introduced Muse. Both AI agents use advanced AI models to work autonomously for tasks. They can even email or remind users when new messages arrive. Apple's disclosure comes after several episodes that involved rogue AI agents breaking out of their sandboxes to hack third-party websites, like the Hugging Face incident, which has drawn renewed attention from policymakers in Washington, D.C., and around the world. Separately, the ability of agents to use a computer in human ways is forcing big companies like Amazon and JPMorgan Chase to come up with policies around agentic access to services for strategic or security reasons. Last month, Apple announced changes to full disk access on Macs to reduce "risks related to this level of access" for AI agents installed on PCs. "The Company's ability to oversee and control third-party artificial intelligence agents and other technologies may be limited," Apple warned in its filing. Apple doesn't currently have an agentic AI. But when new CEO John Ternus was asked on Monday's earnings call about AI agents, he said that the company had "real room" to expand Siri's capabilities. "As far as agentic capabilities, we think these are promising tools for users," Ternus said. "We just want to make sure that users are aware of what they are giving access to. We want to make sure this is done in a way that protects security and privacy." This fall, Apple released Siri AI, a new assistant that uses the iPhone's local data storage to access data like calendars and emails, but Apple's Siri can't work autonomously for long stretches like Dots or Muse. Ternus said Apple can't access private data on its devices, calling it a "core differentiator." "If you think about it, so much of your personal data is on your iPhone, whether it's your contacts, your communications, health data, financial data, all of that," Ternus said. "Siri can tap into that and help you access it in a way that's very secure and private and that nobody else has access to." Commercial AI agents like those from OpenAI and Meta ask for high-level access to the user's accounts like email in order to be more useful. Apple indicated that the current regulations around AI and "super intelligence" are changing, unpredictable and that it could cost a lot of money to adapt to new laws governing AI. "In addition, the Company is subject to the risks posed by ethical concerns and negative consumer perceptions related to automation, artificial intelligence and super intelligence, including perceived threats to safety or other societal harms or complications," according to the filing.

The jump from its own prior model is enormous. On Terminal-Bench v2.1, a benchmark that tests an AI agent's ability to complete real command-line tasks, LongCat-2.5 scored 88.4, up from 70.8 for LongCat-2.0. On DeepSWE v1.1, a tougher agentic coding benchmark, it posted 64.6 against LongCat-2.0's 9.7. That's a nearly sevenfold gain in under three months. Meituan is China's largest food delivery company, the one that sends scooters weaving through Beijing traffic to drop off hot pot and bubble tea. The model is natively multimodal, meaning it processes text and images through the same underlying token system instead of bolting a separate vision module on top. LLMs.content: [Artificial Intelligence](/category/artificial-intelligence) # Better Search Pushed an Agent From 36% to 98% Mixedbread showed on AI Engineer how visual late interaction search lifted a hedge fund agent from 36% to 98% accuracy and cut LLM spend by 3x. [![Daniel Singer](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocLFxHdAP6IU1UuAGSDPHMK3W6verITBMnYXo2Kk33EXwjmKG3O9=s96-c)](/author/daniel-singer) By [Daniel Singer](/author/daniel-singer), Editor, StartupHub.ai ·4 min read Better Search Pushed an Agent From 36% to 98%Daniel Singer · Nov 3, 2026 · 4 min read ![Aamir Shakir presenting Mixedbread retrieval demo on stage](https://cdn.startuphub.ai/storage/v1/object/public/post-images/youtube/1793693774658.webp) Credit: AI Engineer Can search alone make a bad agent good? Aamir Shakir said it can, and he showed how on [AI Engineer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Ad73Onx3Aw), where the Mixedbread co-founder demoed a retrieval system that lifted a hedge fund agent from 36% to 98% answer accuracy without changing the underlying language model. ![Better Search Pushed an Agent From 36% to 98% - AI Engineer](https://img.youtube.com/vi/3Ad73Onx3Aw/maxresdefault.jpg) Better Search Pushed an Agent From 36% to 98%, AI Engineer The fix targets budget and workflow, not intelligence. Shakir framed the problem as access, not reasoning. Retrieval-augmented generation is a method that fetches your own documents to ground an agent answer, but the usual stack is what he called a Frankenstein stack. You parse PDFs, run OCR on scans, chunk pages, embed each chunk into a single vector, then search a vector database and rerank. Each step is lossy, he said, and combining vendors for OCR, chunking, embeddings and storage means teams spend six to eight months evaluating tools and assigning four to five people to build what remains brittle. He illustrated it with an equity analyst asking why Intel's new D270 GPU uses LPDDR5 instead of HBM. With lexical search like grep or a single embedding point per chunk, a system returns many near-identical hits and the model must read every candidate. At billions of documents, Shakir said, that pushes a single simple question to $10 or $20 in token cost, and PDFs with tables, figures and scans often are not grepable at all. A single embedding also struggles when documents look alike, he argued, like [Nvidia](https://www.startuphub.ai/ai-news/artificial-intelligence/2026/dell-nvidia-ceos-on-ai-factories-and-china) SEC filings from 1996, 2000 and 2026 whose points collapse together, so quality degrades as the corpus scales and agents compensate by spinning up tens of sub-agents and flooding the context window. What changed is the embedding design. A late interaction model is a retriever that keeps multiple embeddings per page for the document and multiple embeddings per query, so fine grained facts stay distinct while remaining contextualized. Shakir said Mixedbread's next model, previewed for release next week and already live with some customers, creates those embeddings from the visual page itself rather than OCR text, which preserves tables and figures. In a live demo he queried Intel foundry segment operating margin for Q2 2025 and the system returned the exact page at sub-200 millisecond latency with bounding boxes to cite the source. For complex qualitative questions like whether Intel's foundry profitability is improving and why, he said Mixedbread trained an agentic search primitive that decomposes the request into multi-hop queries, which he described as as good as Astra and Fable while being 40 times faster and cheaper. The team also exposes layout and OCR outputs for downstream models that are not yet multimodal, so builders can choose to feed the screenshot or text. The impact shows up in deployment, not just benchmarks. LLMs.content: # [opensource.google.com](https://opensource.google.com/ "Google Open Source") [Menu](/#Navigation "Nav Toggle Open") ## [Google Open Source Blog](/ "Google Open Source Blog") The latest news from Google on open source releases, major projects, events, and outreach programs for early career developers. ## Posts from November 2026 ### [Introducing Three-Live: turning AI-generated Three.js into interactive 3D, AR, and WebXR across web and mobile](https://opensource.googleblog.com/2026/11/introducing-three-live-ai-generated-3d-ar-webxr.html) #### Tuesday, November 3, 2026 ![Screenshot of the Three-Live interactive studio running in a browser, showing live procedural Three.js controls and a real-time PBR 3D scene with metallic and emissive materials.](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEicVnawvU2wNMNMemlGTdmQ0lERS9IupQ4HCSTUDQsm7BAarw2YSunm4XK_QbZuF3NgHTe56q1cBYnPbVj4YK6vXftiv44SvgYGOuS0eWeHaWhhv3WRRgys-sHmEVUVlbXbVx3CWPHgz9Yi4S8S-2MQVSEEwTiOJger-yAToVWGxyrG1CRwTTK3DU5UM9E/s1600/image.png) by Jonathan Bingham, AI Foundations Want to add AI-generated 3D or XR to your web or mobile app? Unsure how to get started? That’s why we created the open source cross-platform project Three-Live—written entirely by [Google Antigravity](https://antigravity.google/), in partnership with one former software engineer turned product manager. *(Three-Live is not an officially supported Google product.)* You can think of Three-Live as a simple, unofficial companion to the more capable and feature-rich [XR Blocks](https://xrblocks.github.io/), Android XR’s web-based cross-platform framework for XR. The goal of Three-Live is to make it easy to get started with 3D and XR that’s AI-authored in [Three.js](https://threejs.org/). Three-Live combines the familiar developer experience of and native mobile libraries with a sandboxed compiler for on-device or server-side compilation of untrusted LLM-generated JavaScript. Large language models (LLMs) have gotten remarkably good at writing software, and that includes generating 3D code in procedural [Three.js](https://threejs.org/) JavaScript that describes objects, materials, lighting, and animations. But runtime AI-generated code is not trusted, and requires security sandboxing for safe execution. Also, mobile devices provide native support for 3D and XR rendering, and forcing them to run a webview limits the performance. [![Screenshot of the Three-Live interactive studio running in a browser, showing live procedural Three.js controls and a real-time PBR 3D scene with metallic and emissive materials.](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEicVnawvU2wNMNMemlGTdmQ0lERS9IupQ4HCSTUDQsm7BAarw2YSunm4XK_QbZuF3NgHTe56q1cBYnPbVj4YK6vXftiv44SvgYGOuS0eWeHaWhhv3WRRgys-sHmEVUVlbXbVx3CWPHgz9Yi4S8S-2MQVSEEwTiOJger-yAToVWGxyrG1CRwTTK3DU5UM9E/s1600/image.png)](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEicVnawvU2wNMNMemlGTdmQ0lERS9IupQ4HCSTUDQsm7BAarw2YSunm4XK_QbZuF3NgHTe56q1cBYnPbVj4YK6vXftiv44SvgYGOuS0eWeHaWhhv3WRRgys-sHmEVUVlbXbVx3CWPHgz9Yi4S8S-2MQVSEEwTiOJger-yAToVWGxyrG1CRwTTK3DU5UM9E/s1600/image.png) Today, we are excited to release [Three-Live](https://github.com/google/three-live) (`v1.0.0`, Developer Preview) under the Apache 2.0 license. It’s a lightweight, cross-platform open source library and on-device compiler that bridges the gap between AI-generated Three.js code and high-performance 3D, AR, and WebXR rendering across web, Android, and iOS. LLMs.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Holdings](/stocklist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast)[Market Influencers](/influencer) # Chinese AI Models' Price Edge Loses Its Bite as Private Benchmarks Widen the Gap [Add preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) A revamped, partly confidential testing system from Artificial Analysis shows the best open-weight AI models trailing Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 by 12 points, up from a three-point gap under the old benchmarks, suggesting Chinese systems may be less competitive than advertised. Chinese models still account for 65% of tokens but only 29% of spending on OpenRouter, and Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro matches leading coding scores at a fraction of the price. Fund manager Tal Schwartz warns that Chinese price competition could cut U.S. lab revenue by about 13% in a severe scenario, with knock-on risk for AI and semiconductor ETFs and for Nvidia's concentrated customer base. Usage data and Moonshot's own capacity constraints temper the threat. ##### Key Elements ![Chinese AI Models' Price Edge Loses Its Bite as Private Benchmarks Widen the Gap](https://img.biggo.com/pMz1UJmnYB-Y3f7BAarSvCV9G7i0vgz5ux1S0Oyac64/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTExLzkwYzI0MTBjLTAzNmEtNDdhMC04MmUyLWFhMjhkYWI4Njc3Nl8xNzkzNzEzMzY2X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) The argument that cheap Chinese artificial intelligence models will undercut the economics of the U.S. AI boom is running into harder evidence, as an independent testing overhaul shows open-weight systems trailing America's leaders by a wider margin than previously measured. Artificial Analysis, a research firm that ranks AI models, recently rebuilt its evaluation system to mirror real-world use and, critically, to keep many of the underlying tests confidential. Under the prior setup, the strongest open-weight models sat about three points behind the overall leader. With the new tests in place, that shortfall stretched to 12 points, according to the firm. The revised scores put Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at 58 points among models with publicly released weights, against 32 for the best open models, a group that includes Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro. Even a smaller Anthropic model, Claude Haiku 5.5, outscored every model whose weights are freely downloadable. The methodology change matters because public benchmarks let developers tune their systems to the specific questions being asked, a practice Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and others have labeled "benchmark hacking." Sridhar Ramaswamy, chief executive of Snowflake and a former Google executive, flagged the shift in a post on X: "The day benchmarks went private, the open-model gap went from 3 points to 12. Were open models catching up, or was the test leaking?" Nathan Lambert, cofounder of Trillium Labs, which studies large language models with an emphasis on open-weight systems, conceded that the earlier index had been too generous. "I do think the previous index was flattering the open weight models too strongly," he said. He added that open models remain competitive in software development and can give businesses more control and lower costs. The pricing threat has not vanished. Tal Schwartz, founder of Ai Funds, which runs the Ai Funds High Conviction US Equity AI-Managed ETF (BATS:HIAI), told Benzinga that disappointing monetization driven by what he called Chinese "AI dumping" ranks among the biggest hazards for the sector. The tools are intended to address a problem many businesses face as they deploy AI agents across different systems, clouds and data platforms. Snowflake cited research it sponsored with MIT Technology Review Insights, which found that 55% of executives saw a lack of business context as the main cause of poor-quality AI agent insights, while 45% pointed to fragmented or inaccessible data. ![](/uploads/ckeditor/attachments/4243/Cortex_AI_Gateway.webp) Business Ontology, part of Snowflake Horizon Catalog, is designed to give organisations a single governed source for official business definitions. This is intended to help agents return answers based on approved meanings for terms such as net revenue, rather than conflicting interpretations drawn from separate dashboards, analysts or data dictionaries. The feature links those definitions to the tables and views that implement them across data held inside and outside Snowflake. Every change is logged, creating an audit trail that shows what a term meant at a given time and who approved it. Snowflake said the product works alongside Semantic View, which handles how a term is calculated, and Cortex Sense, which infers operational knowledge that has not been formally documented. Together, these elements create a shared business context for agents, applications and staff. Christian Kleinerman, Executive Vice President of Product at Snowflake, set out the company's position on governance in AI deployments. "For decades, governance gave organizations the confidence to make decisions with correctness, security and compliance. In the agentic era, governance is no different: it promotes trust and accelerates AI adoption. The enterprises that win won't be the ones with the most agents. They'll be the ones whose agents know exactly what the business means, access the right data, abide by specified governance and guardrails, and can account for actions taken. By extending Snowflake Horizon Catalog with Business Ontology and Cortex AI Gateway, context and governance stop being afterthoughts and become the foundation every agent is built on for the agentic enterprise," Kleinerman said. **Shared definitions** Some early users said the appeal lies in replacing static dictionaries with centrally maintained definitions that AI systems can use directly. "The value of a data product depends on everyone agreeing what each attribute means, whether it's a household income band or a B2B firmographic segment. Sam Altman met with Abu Dhabi's Crown Prince, and the agreements will bring OpenAI's technology into government services, energy, investments, and education. The 4 deals cover some of the country's most important sectors. 1. Government: AI will help interpret laws, review permits, and process regulatory paperwork. The first system is already running. 2. Energy: State-owned oil giant ADNOC will use OpenAI to optimize oil production, operations, and commercial decisions. 3. Investments: Sovereign wealth fund Mubadala will use AI to analyze investment opportunities and risks. 4. Education and business: A five-year agreement with G42's Inception42 will expand AI adoption across the UAE. Its first pilot is already running for food imports, with officials retaining final authority. Abu Dhabi has already committed around $3.5 billion to its 2025-2027 government digital transformation strategy, aiming to automate all government processes and introduce more than 200 AI solutions. Now zoom out for a moment. We're talking about an American AI company becoming deeply involved in another country's government, oil industry, investment decisions, and education system. The UAE will retain control over its decisions, with AI processing taking place locally. But just a few years ago, it would have been hard to imagine a government inviting a foreign technology company this deeply into its most important institutions. And it makes you realize how powerful these AI companies could become, and how much influence their technology may have over entire economies and governments. Whatever happens to AI valuations, this level of adoption could change how entire countries operate for decades. Open Source AI.title: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models' identity | TechCrunch
Open Source AI.titleZh: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models' identity | TechCrunch
Open Source AI.content: Anthropic is working on an open-source system to verify which AI model produced a given output, according to a blog post published Tuesday. The system, called FlashProve, is built to provide what researchers call “provable inference” – a cryptographic proof, essentially a mathematical guarantee, that a given output came from a specific model. It’s meant to let users confirm that the answer they received really came from the model they think they’re using. Similar to cryptographic email signatures that let recipients confirm a message really came from its claimed sender, FlashProve would be robust against impostors attempting to disguise one model as another, even when the impostor is the lab that built and runs the model. In particular, the researchers note that the system could be used to prevent an AI company from secretly swapping in a cheaper model to cut costs, or a more expensive model to inflate its performance results. FlashProve could also be used to verify claims by third parties that a specific task was done by an advanced model. “A developer might claim that their software library was scanned for vulnerabilities by a frontier cybersecurity model, or a company might claim that its business plan was given the go-ahead by an appropriate model,” the researchers write. “How can a user verify these claims?” To work, the system requires AI labs to publish a “fingerprint” of each model they release that can later be matched to specific outputs and verified cryptographically. Crucially, the fingerprints don’t reveal a model’s weights, the internal numbers that define how it behaves and which closed-model makers like Anthropic and OpenAI keep private. That means labs could publish the fingerprints without giving up their most valuable asset, enabling the system to work with commercial models, too. The system is also designed to be lightweight, so verification could be performed on a local device. As part of the announcement, researchers released a detailed technical specification and working code for various elements of the system, which is publicly available under an open-source license on GitHub. Research in the system is ongoing, and there are no plans to deploy it at Anthropic or any other lab. “This research post is meant to share intermediate progress, and not a completed research agenda,” researchers explain in the announcement post. “We are sharing this explicitly with the goal that others look at what we have done, take it, and improve it.” Topics When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. The jump from its own prior model is enormous. On Terminal-Bench v2.1, a benchmark that tests an AI agent's ability to complete real command-line tasks, LongCat-2.5 scored 88.4, up from 70.8 for LongCat-2.0. On DeepSWE v1.1, a tougher agentic coding benchmark, it posted 64.6 against LongCat-2.0's 9.7. That's a nearly sevenfold gain in under three months. Meituan is China's largest food delivery company, the one that sends scooters weaving through Beijing traffic to drop off hot pot and bubble tea. It is also, somewhat quietly, building one of the more serious open-weight model labs in the country under its LongCat brand, run separately from the consumer app. LongCat-2.5 is a mixture-of-experts model with 1.6 trillion total parameters, of which only about 48 billion activate for any given task. It's the same scale as its predecessor but retrained for far longer task chains. It handles a million-token context window. It can also output up to 128,000 tokens in a single response, which matters for a model meant to work through an entire codebase rather than one function at a time. The model is natively multimodal, meaning it processes text and images through the same underlying token system instead of bolting a separate vision module on top. Infra & Chips.content: ![]() ![Invezz](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/invezz--theme-light.svg) ![Invezz](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/invezz--theme-dark.svg) # Nvidia tells data center partners to limit China exposure below 50%: report ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg) ![Jensen Huang](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/image/invezz:e53c09b27094b-0d92e7daf13332cdb6119771fa1ebd69-resized.webp) Nvidia NVDA has instructed its data center partners to reduce their exposure to Chinese customers, according to a Financial Times report published Tuesday, amid Washington's increasing efforts to restrict Beijing's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips. The world's largest chipmaker has reportedly told cloud computing partners to ensure that at least 51% of their services are sold to non-Chinese companies. The guidance was communicated verbally through Nvidia's sales teams and regional offices rather than through formal written instructions, the report said. The reported restrictions apply to new contracts and do not affect existing agreements. Nvidia has not officially confirmed the policy. **What has Nvidia told its partners?** The reported requirement would push data center operators to diversify their customer base and reduce the proportion of computing services supplied to Chinese businesses. The development could create additional challenges for Chinese AI companies that have relied on overseas cloud providers to access advanced Nvidia processors. Renting computing capacity outside China has offered these companies an alternative route to using powerful American chips without importing them directly. A follow-up report by The Information said Nvidia's instructions were intended to encourage a broader customer mix and were not being enforced as a mandatory restriction. The distinction suggests the company is seeking greater oversight of how its chips are used. **Nvidia defends American chip infrastructure** America cannot win the AI race unless America's AI infrastructure wins worldwide -- if the world's clouds rely on foreign-made chips, the model and application layers will be foreign-built as well. Nvidia neither confirmed nor denied the report. However, the company emphasized the importance of expanding the global reach of American-built AI infrastructure. "Datacenters and clouds built on American chips are the foundation that American model and application makers need to compete worldwide," the company said in a statement cited by AFP. It added that America's ability to compete in AI depends on its infrastructure being widely adopted across global cloud networks. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told AFP that she was unaware of the reported restrictions. She added that Beijing hopes companies from all countries will receive a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory business environment. **Nvidia under scanner** The reported move comes as Washington continues to restrict exports of advanced AI processors to China, citing national security concerns and the potential military applications of the technology. Last week, a New York Times investigation reported that US intelligence officials suspected a Chinese businesswoman associated with Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed of passing commercial information to Beijing. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had reportedly developed a close relationship with the executive. Nvidia has said their interactions were routine business meetings. Separately, a contractor linked to server maker Super Micro pleaded guilty in October to participating in a scheme to illegally divert Nvidia-powered AI servers to China. Prosecutors allege that there are two others associated with Super Micro, including a co-founder of the AI-server ​maker, who conspired to divert about $2.5 billion worth of US AI technology to China in violation ​of export laws. ## [NVDA chart](/chart/?symbol=NASDAQ%3ANVDA) ## [Latest news](/news-flow) ## [More news from Invezz](/news-flow/?provider=inve...

NEW DELHI: [E2E Networks](/tag/e2e+networks) on Tuesday has launched Blaze, a pay-per-token inference service for open AI models. The service provides developers and enterprises with a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint to leading open models. Blaze runs on [Nvidia](/tag/nvidia) [GPU infrastructure](/tag/gpu+infrastructure) and open-source components from [Nvidia DSX OS](/tag/nvidia+dsx+os). It turns E2E’s India-hosted [AI factory](/tag/ai+factory) capacity into production inference services, with customers paying only for the tokens they use. The move comes as Indian AI companies move from pilots to production, making inference cost and latency critical to product viability as AI agents drive up token consumption. Advt “Blaze is where you can run your production inference,” said Tarun Dua, founder and managing director, E2E Networks. He added that there is customer demand for frontier-class open-weight models running on an Nvidia Cloud Partner (NCP) with Nvidia reference design clusters as [Sovereign Compute](/tag/sovereign+compute). Blaze is designed for inference-heavy products where latency and cost per token matter most, including voice, coding agents, document AI and OCR, image and video generation, and language applications. ### Award #### [ETTelecom Awards 2027](https://telecom.economictimes.indiatimes.com/telecom-awards?ag=whats_happening&utm_source=whats_happening&utm_co...

Infra & Chips.content: ![](https://sb.scorecardresearch.com/p?c1=2&c2=16433046&cv=3.9.1&cj=1) ## ## Latest in ## More # Is Nvidia a Buy Right Now? ## Key Points The market is worried that the AI infrastructure boom could be in its late stages. Nvidia remains the largest supplier of GPU chip for AI data centers. Nvidia's stock is already priced for slowing growth, making it a potential buy for long-term investors ahead of its Q3 earnings report this month. The stakes are high this earnings season. Investors are paying close attention to how changes in the debt markets and capital expenditures might impact the artificial intelligence (AI) trade. Fears about a possible slowdown in the AI build-out have already stoked a broad sell-off across AI infrastructure stocks, including data center GPU kingpin **Nvidia**(NASDAQ: NVDA), which now sits about 15% below its all-time high. ***Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger.** Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Here's what matters as we approach a very important earnings report. ## The pressure is starting to build even more At this point, Nvidia is probably used to the pressure of being the face of the AI infrastructure trade. But as speculation rises over whether funding will dry up for companies building all these data centers -- you know, Nvidia's customers -- the pressure is going to turn up even more. ![Nvidia company graphic.](https://barchart-news-media-prod.aws.barchart.com/FC/173fc6619cefb8dbb5cdb55e5e49e0f6/%3Furl%3Dhttps%253a%252f%252fg.foolcdn.com%252feditorial%252fimages%252f888176%252fnvidia-company-graphic.png%26amp%3Bw%3D700) Image source: The Motley Fool. Nvidia guided for $108 billion in third-quarter revenue, implying 106% year-over-year growth. Consider what it would look like if Nvidia's Q3 sales come in softer than Wall Street expects. It could easily lend credibility to the notion that the infrastructure trade has peaked, which would require investors to more closely scrutinize the sector's growth expectations. ## Nvidia's valuation has a buffer against slowing growth Right now, Nvidia trades at approximately 23 times this year's estimated earnings. Several years of explosive growth have set a high bar for the company. Analysts have routinely posited that Nvidia would deliver long-term annualized earnings growth as high as 40% to 50%. Buying the stock here at 23 times earnings would probably look like a no-brainer in hindsight if the company actually grows that quickly. And it might. But analysts have begun to lower their expectations as concerns about the state of the infrastructure trade rise. Some analysts now expect Nvidia's earnings to grow at 14% annually over the next three to five years. That would clearly be a major slowdown. The good news for investors is that Nvidia at 23 times earnings is still arguably a solid buy at that growth rate. ## Zooming out can help investors see the big picture It's anyone's guess where Nvidia's numbers will land when earnings drop, and nobody can know how the market might react.
